items.label: 1C
items.claim: Natera's non-oncology tests (mostly NIPT and women's health) have been accelerating for four straight quarters, from +4.6% to +12.5% y/y, so there is no NIPT-maturation drag at Illumina's largest clinical customer.
items.detail: Non-oncology is total tests processed minus oncology tests processed, from the 8-K Ex. 99.1 releases. Q1'24 621.0K and Q1'25 687.4K (+10.7%). Q2'24 634.9K and Q2'25 664.3K (+4.6%). Q3'24 638.7K and Q3'25 682.6K (+6.9%). Q4'24 642.0K and Q4'25 690.3K (+7.5%). Q1'26 754.7K (+9.8%). Q2'26 747.2K (+12.5%). The trough was Q2'25 and growth has risen each quarter since. This corrects the known '+5-7% through 2025' (F131), because Q1'25 was +10.7% and the 2025 average is about +7%. In Q2'26 the seasonal q/q change was −1.0%, against −3.4% in Q2'25 and +2.2% in Q2'24. Management also said women's health grew high-single-digit on a seasonally adjusted basis.
items.source_name: Natera 8-K Ex. 99.1 test volume tables (Q1'25, Q2'25, Q3'25, Q4'25, Q1'26, Q2'26)
items.why_new: Gives the full quarterly non-oncology y/y series and shows re-acceleration; the known file only has a vague '+10-12% H1'26' and a '+5-7%' 2025 figure.

items.label: 1C
items.claim: Natera's clinical MRD unit adds were steady at +20K to +24K per quarter, and the Q2'26 record +34K was flattered by weather-suppressed Q1 volumes, with management guiding no new record in Q3.
items.detail: Clinical MRD units: Q1'25 161K, Q2'25 ~181K (+20K), Q3'25 202K (+21.5K), Q4'25 225K (+23K), Q1'26 249K (+24K), Q2'26 283K (+34K). The sequential growth rate is 12.4%, 11.9%, 11.4%, 10.7%, then 13.7%. Over the two quarters Q4'25 to Q2'26, units rose 283/225 = +25.8%, about 12.2% a quarter. That is in line with the prior trend, so the Q2 record is catch-up, not acceleration. On the Q2'26 call management said Q1 weather suppressed volumes, the 34K prior record was 25K, and it does not expect a record in Q3. If adds revert to ~25-29K, the y/y rate drifts from +56% toward the high-40s%, still strong.
items.source_name: Natera Q2'26 call (GuruFocus summary), Q3'25/Q4'25/Q1'26 call summaries and 8-Ks
items.why_new: The known file only has the Q2'26 level (283K, +56%); this adds the full sequential-add series, the q/q % trend and the explicit weather and Q3 caveat.

items.label: 1C
items.claim: Natera's cost of product revenue per test processed keeps rising (+9% to +12% y/y), and management says new products are not yet optimized for cost. Cheaper sequencing is being reinvested in depth and mix, not passed to price.
items.detail: Cost of product revenues divided by total tests processed: Q1'25 $184.6M/855.1K = $215.9; Q1'26 $245.2M/1,013.6K = $241.9 (+12.0%); Q2'25 $199.5M/853.1K = $233.9; Q2'26 $266.6M/1,043.9K = $255.4 (+9.2%). Q1'26 includes an equity charge from the Foresight integration that management put at about 2 points of margin. On the Q2'26 call, management said COGS rose slightly on Fetal Focus, LATITUDE and Signatera Genome volumes, with 12-18 months of COGS projects to come. Product revenue per test rose faster, from $638 to $716 (+12.3%), so margin held.
items.source_name: Natera Q2'26 10-Q, Q1'26 8-K, Q2'26 call (Investing.com/Yahoo summaries)
items.why_new: Adds the Q1'26 +12% cost-per-test datapoint and management's explicit attribution to Signatera Genome and other new launches; the known file only has the Q2 +9%.

items.label: 1C
items.claim: Natera's accrual for 'testing and laboratory materials from suppliers' more than doubled in H1'26, a consumables-spend signal that points to rising volume at Illumina's largest customer.
items.detail: The Q2'26 10-Q shows the accrual at $30.9M against $12.4M at 31 Dec 2025 (+150% in six months). Over the same period inventory of supplies rose from $68.4M to $80.3M (+17%). Gross machinery and equipment rose from $170.6M to $214.8M, and construction-in-process from $94.0M to $131.1M. The accrual is not split by supplier, so it is not Illumina-specific.
items.why_new: Balance-sheet capacity and supplies data not in the known file; it corroborates the Austin build-out already noted.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: Natera's total material supplier purchase commitments fell to $220.5M at 30 Jun 2026 from $256.9M, with the largest block ($120.3M) running to Nov 2030. That is consistent with no growing hard commitment to a single sequencing vendor.
items.detail: The 10-Q lists total material commitments of $220.5M: material suppliers $120.3M (to Nov 2030), other material suppliers $48.3M, lab instruments $13.4M (Dec 2027), cloud $22.7M and application services $15.9M. The known FY25 10-K figure is $256.9M, so commitments fell about 14% while tests grew 22% y/y. The line does not name Illumina. Commitments below volume growth mean Natera is not locking in volume-based pricing through commitments, which leaves its leverage with the supply-agreement terms (the Eleventh Amendment).
items.why_new: Updates the known $256.9M commitment figure to Q2'26 and shows the 2030 maturity of the largest block.

items.label: 1C
items.claim: Oncology is now 28% of Natera's tests, up from 16% two years ago. Test counts understate Gb growth because Natera's oncology tests need more sequencing than its women's health tests.
items.detail: Oncology share of total tests processed: Q1'24 114.8K/735.8K = 15.6%; Q2'24 125.4/760.3 = 16.5%; Q4'24 150.8/792.8 = 19.0%; Q2'25 188.8/853.1 = 22.1%; Q4'25 233.3/923.6 = 25.3%; Q2'26 296.7/1,043.9 = 28.4%. Oncology grew 50-57% in each of the last 8 quarters. Within oncology, the rest after clinical MRD units (Prospera, Empower, biopharma and other) rose from 6.7K (Q1'25) to 13.7K (Q2'26), and from 9.9K in Q1'26 (+38% q/q). The company does not disclose biopharma Signatera separately.
items.why_new: Gives the quarterly oncology-share series and a derived non-clinical-MRD oncology residual; the known file has only the 28% endpoint.

items.label: 1C
items.claim: Women's health at Natera is gaining share after the enhanced Panorama launch, so NIPT looks less like a maturing drag at the largest NIPT lab.
items.detail: On the Q2'26 call the CFO said women's health grew high-single-digit on a seasonally adjusted basis versus Q2'25, helped by new account wins and early results from the enhanced Panorama test. The test cuts the no-call rate to 0.5%, and Fetal Focus adoption helped. The CEO said Natera is 'definitely benefiting from share gains in women's health'. Share gains at one lab mean some of the volume is taken from other NIPT labs (Labcorp, BillionToOne), so the market itself may be growing more slowly.
items.source_name: Natera Q2'26 earnings call (GuruFocus and Fool summaries)
items.quote: definitely benefiting from share gains in women's health
items.why_new: Adds management's seasonally adjusted women's health growth rate, the 0.5% no-call figure and the share-gain framing, none of which are in the known file.

notes: Mined 8-K Ex. 99.1 for Q1'24 through Q2'26 (Q1'24 and Q2'24 via the prior-year comparisons in the 2025 releases). Not done: Q3'24 and earlier clinical MRD unit counts, the Q1'26 and Q2'26 10-Q MD&A (the fetch stopped before Item 2), and the full Q2'26 Q&A. No source gave a clinical vs biopharma Signatera split, reads per test or Signatera Genome volume. Natera does not disclose them, and Signatera Genome is only named as a COGS-unoptimized launch. Natera does not name a sequencer on the call. One page fetch (the Fool transcript) returned text saying it treated my query as page text, so I did not act on it and used only the factual content. The fetched summaries are secondary, so quotes should be checked against the transcripts. The Q1'26 8-K shows 258.9K oncology tests processed, against 249K clinical oncology in the investor deck, and the gap is the residual used above.
